references.text: Matthew's parallel account of when Jesus came to the country of the Gadarenes and met the demon-possessed men. Matthew uses the name 'Gadarenes' area, while Luke uses 'Gerasenes', but it concerns the same event.
Mark's parallel account of the demon-possessed man in the country of the Gerasenes. Mark gives the most detailed version of this event and uses the same place name as Luke.

The preceding account where Jesus calmed the storm on the sea, which took place just before they sailed over to the country of the Gerasenes. The crossing to the other side of the Sea of Galilee is the direct background for the arrival in verse 26.
Jesus gave orders to cross to the other side of the lake, resulting in the journey that led them to the country of the Gerasenes.
Mark's version of Jesus' command to cross to the other side of the lake, which led to their arrival in the Gentile region on the eastern side of the Sea of Galilee.
